1. # recodeAgent — multi-agent Python→Rust translation of xcvrd
2. 
3. A ReCodeAgent-style (arXiv:2604.07341) multi-agent pipeline that translates the
4. SONiC **xcvrd** transceiver daemon from Python to Rust, validating every step as
5. a **black box** against the existing `xcvrd-tests` suite on the `sonic-dev`
6. testbed.
7. 
8. The LLM work is done by **GitHub Copilot CLI custom agents** (Analyzer, Planner,
9. Translator, Validator). A small **Apache Burr** state machine is the only
10. deterministic code: it sequences the agents, owns the milestone × repair loop,
11. persists state (crash-resume), and renders the live graph UI. Burr never calls an
12. LLM — Copilot is the agent runtime.
13. 
14. > **Scope boundary:** everything here lives under `dev/recodeAgent/`. The pipeline
15. > *calls* `xcvrd-tests/run.sh` and drives the DUT over SSH, but never edits
16. > `xcvrd-tests/`, `platform/`, `emu-deploy/`, `xcvr-emu/`, or
17. > `setup-sonic-testbed.sh`.
18. 
19. ---
20. 
21. ## 0. Quickstart — install agents & run the app
22. 
23. From **Git Bash** in `dev/recodeAgent/` (Python ≥ 3.11):
24. 
25. ```bash
26. # 1. Install the orchestrator (Apache Burr) — once
27. pip install -e .                    # add '.[tracking]' for Burr telemetry, '.[ui]' for the UI
28.                                     # (without [tracking] the run still works; the tracker just auto-disables)
29. 
30. # 2. Install the six Copilot custom-agent profiles into $COPILOT_HOME/agents
31. bash tools/install_agents.sh        # copilot.py also auto-installs before each run
32. 
33. # 3a. Offline dry-run — mock agents, no Copilot/DUT, ~30s (proves the graph wiring)
34. export PYTHON=python
35. python -m orchestrator.app --app-id demo --mock
36. 
37. # 3b. Real run — drives the actual LLM agents (needs `copilot login` + AI credits)
38. python -m orchestrator.app --app-id run1
39. ```
40. 
41. `--app-id` is the resume key: re-running the **same** id continues from the last
42. persisted node (crash-resume); use a fresh id to start over. Useful flags:
43. `--max-iter N` (per-milestone repair budget, default 10), `--max-parity-rounds N`
44. (outer parity budget, default 3), `--mock` (offline), `--db PATH` (state file).
45. Installed as a console script too: `recode --app-id run1`. Watch it live with the
46. Burr UI: `burr` → open the printed URL → project `recodeagent-xcvrd` (see §7).
47. 
48. ---
49. 
50. ## 1. Architecture
51. 
52. ```
53. Apache Burr  (deterministic state machine + telemetry UI + SQLite resume)
54.   analyze ─▶ scope ─▶ plan ─▶ select_milestone ─▶ translate ─▶ validate
55.               ▲                     ▲                   ▲            │
56.    re-scope   │        next milestone │        repair    │          │ parse results.xml
57.    (parity    │        (passed &      │        (failed & │          ▼
58.     gaps)     │         more left)    │         iter<max)│      verdict
59.               │                       └───────────────────┴──────────┤
60.               │                              all milestones green ─▶ parity_verify
61.               └──────────────────────── gaps + budget left ──────────┤
62.                                         complete (or budget spent) ─▶ terminal
63.         │ every action = subprocess ▼                 │ validate action ▼
64.    GitHub Copilot CLI custom agents            tools/validate_on_dut.sh
65.    (Opus 4.8, high reasoning)                    build Rust (Debian-13 container)
66.    analyzer / scoper / planner /                 ▶ inject into pmon (reversible)
67.    translator / validator / parity_verifier      ▶ xcvrd-tests/run.sh  (UNCHANGED)
68.    do ALL real work via their tools              ▶ parse results.xml ▶ restore py xcvrd
69. ```
70. 
71. Two nested loops: the **inner** milestone×repair loop (correctness, gated by the e2e
72. oracle) and the **outer** parity loop (completeness). The **Scoper** derives the
73. milestone set from the analysis + the `xcvrd-tests` suite; the **Parity Verifier**
74. compares the finished Rust against the Python source per module and, if anything is
75. untranslated, feeds gaps back to the Scoper as new unit-only milestones. There is **no
76. deferral** — the run succeeds only when parity is complete; exhausting the outer budget
77. with gaps still open is a hard failure.
78. 
79. **Division of labor**
80. 
81. | Layer | Owner | Responsibility |
82. |-------|-------|----------------|
83. | Sequencing, milestone loop, repair loop, parity loop, typed state, resume, UI | **Burr** (this repo) | ~250 lines of deterministic Python |
84. | Analysis, scoping, planning, translation, repair diagnosis, parity check | **Copilot agents** | all the LLM reasoning + code writing |
85. | Black-box verdict | **`xcvrd-tests/run.sh`** (unchanged) | trusted oracle; `results.xml` is the structured result |
86. | HAL + STATE_DB + build/deploy | **environment scaffolding** (this repo) | provided so agents don't fight interop (see §3) |
87. 
88. ---
89. 
90. ## 2. How we adapt the paper (deliberately)
91. 
92. Faithful to ReCodeAgent's agents and Algorithm 1 loop, extended with two agents of
93. our own (**Scoper**, **Parity Verifier**) and these adaptations for our environment:
94. 
95. 1. **Two validation layers — unit tests (Part B) *and* a fixed black-box oracle.**
96.    We keep the paper's Part B (test translation): the Translator rewrites xcvrd's

 ### 3b. STATE_DB = official `swss-common` Rust crate
 
 The Rust daemon reads/writes Redis STATE_DB through the upstream Rust bindings at
 [`sonic-net/sonic-swss-common` `crates/swss-common`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss-common/tree/master/crates/swss-common/src),
 not a hand-rolled client. It's a **pinned git dependency** (`xcvrd-rs/Cargo.toml`,
 rev `7faca59`) exposing `DbConnector`, `Table`, `SonicV2Connector`,
 `ProducerStateTable`, `SubscriberStateTable`, etc. Agents write STATE_DB from Rust
 with e.g. `DbConnector::new_unix(6, "/var/run/redis/redis.sock", 0)?.hset(key, field, &CxxString::from(v))`.
 
 **Native-lib wiring (the tricky part, solved once):** `swss-common`'s `build.rs`
 runs **bindgen** over the C-API headers and links `dylib=swsscommon` (the C++
 `libswsscommon`). pmon ships `libswsscommon.so.0` **with the C-API compiled in**

 Rust binary loads and runs there. The build container (`Dockerfile.build`) bakes

 `tools/dut/ensure_swsslib.sh` and mounted at build time (`-L native=/swsslib`).
 Keep the `Dockerfile.build` `SWSS_COMMON_REV` arg in sync with the Cargo rev.

 | 5 | Parity feedback loop | parity `passed=False`, Scoper appends `M7` (origin parity), then `done=True parity_round=2` |

1. //! xcvrd-rs bootstrap library.
2. //!
3. //! This is the starting point the ReCodeAgent translation pipeline builds on. The
4. //! two environment bindings the daemon needs are already wired as dependencies, so
5. //! agents can `use` them directly and never re-solve interop:
6. //!
7. //!   - [`platform_bridge`] — the Python `sonic_platform` HAL (xcvr-emu) via PyO3.
8. //!     `Platform`/`Chassis`/`Sfp` expose `get_transceiver_info`, `get_change_event`,
9. //!     DOM/status, lpmode/reset, eeprom, … (CMIS decode stays in Python).
10. //!   - [`swss_common`] — STATE_DB (Redis) via the official sonic-net bindings.
11. //!     `DbConnector`, `Table`, `ProducerStateTable`, `SubscriberStateTable`, …
12. //!
13. //! [`env`] gives ready-made constructors ([`env::open_platform`],
14. //! [`env::open_state_db`]) so daemon code has one documented place to obtain a HAL
15. //! handle and a STATE_DB connection. Agents grow this module into the real
16. //! platform/DB layer as the milestones (see the repo README §5) require.
17. //!
18. //! Runnable demonstrations live in `examples/` (build with `cargo build
19. //! --examples`, or `bash tools/env_check.sh` to run them inside pmon):
20. //!   - `statedb_probe`   — STATE_DB round-trip via swss-common only.
21. //!   - `hal_to_statedb`  — the agent pattern: read a transceiver via the bridge,
22. //!                          then publish it to STATE_DB (what `SfpStateUpdateTask`
23. //!                          will do for real).
24. 
25. //! ## Translation skeleton (ReCodeAgent Planner)
26. //!
27. //! Beyond the M0/M1 bootstrap ([`daemon`] + [`env`]), the crate now carries the
28. //! stubbed module tree that mirrors the Python `xcvrd` package (analysis §3.3):
29. //!
30. //!   - [`hal`] / [`db`] — the two mockable trait seams (HAL over `platform-bridge`,
31. //!     STATE_DB over `swss-common`); [`mock`] provides the test doubles (the Rust
32. //!     analogue of `tests/mock_platform.py` / `tests/mock_swsscommon.py`).
33. //!   - [`xcvrd`] — `DaemonXcvrd` + `SfpStateUpdateTask` (presence/identity).
34. //!   - [`cmis`] — `CmisManagerTask` (datapath bring-up).
35. //!   - [`dom`] — `DomInfoUpdateTask`/`DomThermalInfoUpdateTask` + the DOM/status/VDM
36. //!     posters under `dom::utilities`.
37. //!   - [`sff_mgr`] — optional `SffManagerTask`.
38. //!   - [`xcvrd_utilities`] — shared helpers (common/table-registry/port-mapping/
39. //!     error-decode/utils/media+optics SI).
40. //!   - [`error`] — the crate `XcvrdError` + `Result` alias.
41. //!
42. //! All bodies are `todo!()` stubs behind clear TODOs; the Translator fills them in
43. //! milestone by milestone (see `pipeline/plan.json`). The bootstrap in [`daemon`]
44. //! keeps M0/M1 green while the tree grows.
45.

47. pub mod env;
48.

51. pub mod hal;
52. pub mod mock;
53. 
54. pub mod cmis;
55. pub mod dom;
56. pub mod sff_mgr;
57. pub mod xcvrd;
58. pub mod xcvrd_utilities;

     def retry_eeprom_reading(self):
         """Retry EEPROM reading, if retry succeed, remove the logical port from the retry set
         """
         if not self.retry_eeprom_set:
             return
 
         # Retry eeprom with an interval RETRY_EEPROM_READING_INTERVAL. No need to put sleep here
         # because _wrapper_get_transceiver_change_event has a timeout argument.
         now = time.time()
         if now - self.last_retry_eeprom_time < self.RETRY_EEPROM_READING_INTERVAL:
             return
 
         self.last_retry_eeprom_time = now
 
         transceiver_dict = {}
         retry_success_set = set()
         for logical_port in self.retry_eeprom_set:
             asic_index = self.port_mapping.get_asic_id_for_logical_port(logical_port)
             rc = post_port_sfp_info_to_db(logical_port, self.port_mapping, self.xcvr_table_helper.get_intf_tbl(asic_index), transceiver_dict)
             if rc != SFP_EEPROM_NOT_READY:
                 self.dom_db_utils.post_port_dom_thresholds_to_db(logical_port)
                 self.vdm_db_utils.post_port_vdm_thresholds_to_db(logical_port)
 
                 media_settings_parser.notify_media_setting(logical_port, transceiver_dict, self.xcvr_table_helper, self.port_mapping)
                 transceiver_dict.clear()
                 retry_success_set.add(logical_port)
         # Update retry EEPROM set
         self.retry_eeprom_set -= retry_success_set

             if update_log_level and callable(update_log_level):
                 thread.update_log_level()

     def signal_handler(self, sig, frame):

         elif sig == signal.SIGINT:

         elif sig == signal.SIGTERM:

189.     def get_state_db_port_table_val_by_key(self, lport, port_mapping, key):
190.         """
191.         Retrieves the value of a key from STATE_DB PORT_TABLE|<lport> for the given logical port
192.         Args:
193.             lport:
194.                 logical port name
195.             port_mapping:
196.                 A PortMapping object
197.             key:
198.                 key for the corresponding value to be retrieved
199.         Returns:
200.             The value of the key if the key is found in STATE_DB PORT_TABLE|<lport>
201.             None otherwise
202.         """
203. 
204.         if port_mapping is None:
205.             helper_logger.log_error("Get value by key from STATE_DB: port_mapping is None "
206.                                     "for lport {}".format(lport))
207.             return None
208. 
209.         asic_index = port_mapping.get_asic_id_for_logical_port(lport)
210.         state_port_table = self.get_state_port_tbl(asic_index)
211.         if state_port_table is None:
212.             helper_logger.log_error("Get value by key from STATE_DB: state_db is None with asic_index {} "
213.                                     "for lport {}".format(asic_index, lport))
214.             return None
215. 
216.         found, state_port_table_fvs = state_port_table.get(lport)
217.         if not found:
218.             helper_logger.log_error("Get value by key from STATE_DB: Unable to find lport {}".format(lport))
219.             return None
220. 
221.         state_port_table_fvs_dict = dict(state_port_table_fvs)
222.         if key not in state_port_table_fvs_dict:
223.             helper_logger.log_error("Get value by key from STATE_DB: Unable to find key {} "
224.                                     "state_port_table_fvs_dict {} for lport {}".format(key, state_port_table_fvs_dict, lport))
225.             return None
226. 
227.         return state_port_table_fvs_dict[key]

249.     def get_gearbox_line_lanes_dict(self):
250.         """
251.         Retrieves the gearbox line lanes dictionary from APPL_DB
252. 
253.         This method scans all ASICs for gearbox interface configurations and extracts
254.         the line_lanes count for each logical port. The line_lanes represent the
255.         number of lanes on the line side (towards the optical module) which is the
256.         correct count to use for CMIS host lane configuration.
257. 
258.         Returns:
259.             dict: A dictionary where:
260.                 - key (str): logical port name (e.g., "Ethernet0")
261.                 - value (int): number of line-side lanes for that port
262. 
263.         Example:
264.             {"Ethernet0": 2, "Ethernet200": 4}
265. 
266.         Note:
267.             - Returns empty dict if no gearbox configuration is found
268.             - Silently skips invalid or malformed entries
269.             - Only processes keys that start with "interface:"
270.         """
271.         gearbox_line_lanes_dict = {}
272.         try:
273.             for asic_id in self.appl_db:
274.                 appl_db = self.appl_db[asic_id]
275.                 gearbox_table = swsscommon.Table(appl_db, "_GEARBOX_TABLE")
276.                 interface_keys = gearbox_table.getKeys()
277.                 for key in interface_keys:
278.                     if key.startswith("interface:"):
279.                         (found, fvs) = gearbox_table.get(key)
280.                         if found:
281.                             fvs_dict = dict(fvs)
282.                             interface_name = fvs_dict.get('name', '')
283.                             line_lanes_str = fvs_dict.get('line_lanes', '')
284.                             if interface_name and line_lanes_str:
285.                                 line_lanes_count = len(line_lanes_str.split(','))
286.                                 gearbox_line_lanes_dict[interface_name] = line_lanes_count
287.                             else:
288.                                 if not interface_name:
289.                                     helper_logger.log_warning("get_gearbox_line_lanes_dict: ASIC {}: Interface {} missing 'name' field".format(asic_id, key))
290.                                 if not line_lanes_str:
291.                                     helper_logger.log_debug("get_gearbox_line_lanes_dict: ASIC {}: Interface {} has empty 'line_lanes' field".format(asic_id, interface_name))
292.         except Exception as e:
293.             helper_logger.log_error("Error in get_gearbox_line_lanes_dict: {}".format(str(e)))
294.             return gearbox_line_lanes_dict

     def get_state_db_port_table_val_by_key(self, lport, port_mapping, key):
         """
         Retrieves the value of a key from STATE_DB PORT_TABLE|<lport> for the given logical port
         Args:
             lport:
                 logical port name
             port_mapping:
                 A PortMapping object
             key:
                 key for the corresponding value to be retrieved
         Returns:
             The value of the key if the key is found in STATE_DB PORT_TABLE|<lport>
             None otherwise
         """
 
         if port_mapping is None:
             helper_logger.log_error("Get value by key from STATE_DB: port_mapping is None "
                                     "for lport {}".format(lport))
             return None
 
         asic_index = port_mapping.get_asic_id_for_logical_port(lport)
         state_port_table = self.get_state_port_tbl(asic_index)
         if state_port_table is None:
             helper_logger.log_error("Get value by key from STATE_DB: state_db is None with asic_index {} "
                                     "for lport {}".format(asic_index, lport))
             return None
 
         found, state_port_table_fvs = state_port_table.get(lport)
         if not found:
             helper_logger.log_error("Get value by key from STATE_DB: Unable to find lport {}".format(lport))
             return None
 
         state_port_table_fvs_dict = dict(state_port_table_fvs)
         if key not in state_port_table_fvs_dict:
             helper_logger.log_error("Get value by key from STATE_DB: Unable to find key {} "
                                     "state_port_table_fvs_dict {} for lport {}".format(key, state_port_table_fvs_dict, lport))
             return None
 
         return state_port_table_fvs_dict[key]
 
     def is_npu_si_settings_update_required(self, lport, port_mapping):
         """
         Checks if NPU SI settings update is required for a module
         Args:
             lport:
                 logical port name
             port_mapping:
                 A PortMapping object
         Returns:
             True if NPU_SI_SETTINGS_SYNC_STATUS_KEY is
                 - not present/accessible from STATE_DB or
                 - set to NPU_SI_SETTINGS_DEFAULT_VALUE
             False otherwise
         """
         npu_si_settings_sync_val = self.get_state_db_port_table_val_by_key(lport,
                                                                             port_mapping, NPU_SI_SETTINGS_SYNC_STATUS_KEY)
 
         # If npu_si_settings_sync_val is None, it can also mean that the key is not present in the table
         return npu_si_settings_sync_val is None or npu_si_settings_sync_val == NPU_SI_SETTINGS_DEFAULT_VALUE
 
     def get_gearbox_line_lanes_dict(self):
         """
         Retrieves the gearbox line lanes dictionary from APPL_DB
 
         This method scans all ASICs for gearbox interface configurations and extracts
         the line_lanes count for each logical port. The line_lanes represent the
         number of lanes on the line side (towards the optical module) which is the
         correct count to use for CMIS host lane configuration.
 
         Returns:
             dict: A dictionary where:
                 - key (str): logical port name (e.g., "Ethernet0")
                 - value (int): number of line-side lanes for that port
 
         Example:
             {"Ethernet0": 2, "Ethernet200": 4}
 
         Note:
             - Returns empty dict if no gearbox configuration is found
             - Silently skips invalid or malformed entries
             - Only processes keys that start with "interface:"
         """
         gearbox_line_lanes_dict = {}
         try:
             for asic_id in self.appl_db:
                 appl_db = self.appl_db[asic_id]
                 gearbox_table = swsscommon.Table(appl_db, "_GEARBOX_TABLE")
                 interface_keys = gearbox_table.getKeys()
                 for key in interface_keys:
                     if key.startswith("interface:"):
                         (found, fvs) = gearbox_table.get(key)
                         if found:
                             fvs_dict = dict(fvs)
                             interface_name = fvs_dict.get('name', '')
                             line_lanes_str = fvs_dict.get('line_lanes', '')
                             if interface_name and line_lanes_str:
                                 line_lanes_count = len(line_lanes_str.split(','))
                                 gearbox_line_lanes_dict[interface_name] = line_lanes_count
                             else:
                                 if not interface_name:
                                     helper_logger.log_warning("get_gearbox_line_lanes_dict: ASIC {}: Interface {} missing 'name' field".format(asic_id, key))
                                 if not line_lanes_str:
                                     helper_logger.log_debug("get_gearbox_line_lanes_dict: ASIC {}: Interface {} has empty 'line_lanes' field".format(asic_id, interface_name))
         except Exception as e:
             helper_logger.log_error("Error in get_gearbox_line_lanes_dict: {}".format(str(e)))
             return gearbox_line_lanes_dict
 
         return gearbox_line_lanes_dict

         if port_change_event.event_type == port_event_helper.PortChangeEvent.PORT_REMOVE:

     def on_remove_logical_port(self, port_change_event):
         pass
 
     def get_dom_polling_from_config_db(self, lport):
         """
             Returns the value of dom_polling field from PORT table in CONFIG_DB
             For non-breakout ports, this function will get dom_polling field from PORT table of lport (subport = 0)
             For breakout ports, this function will get dom_polling field from PORT table of the first subport
             of lport's corresponding breakout group (subport = 1)
 
             Returns:
                 'disabled' if dom_polling is set to 'disabled', otherwise 'enabled'
         """
         dom_polling = 'enabled'
 
         pport_list = self.port_mapping.get_logical_to_physical(lport)
         if not pport_list:
             self.log_warning("Get dom disabled: Got unknown physical port list {} for lport {}".format(pport_list, lport))
             return dom_polling
         pport = pport_list[0]
 
         logical_port_list = self.port_mapping.get_physical_to_logical(pport)
         if logical_port_list is None:
             self.log_warning("Get dom disabled: Got unknown FP port index {}".format(pport))
             return dom_polling
 
         # First logical port corresponds to the first subport
         first_logical_port = logical_port_list[0]
 
         asic_index = self.port_mapping.get_asic_id_for_logical_port(first_logical_port)
         port_tbl = self.xcvr_table_helper.get_cfg_port_tbl(asic_index)
 
         found, port_info = port_tbl.get(first_logical_port)
         if found and 'dom_polling' in dict(port_info):
             dom_polling = dict(port_info)['dom_polling']
 
         return dom_polling

         if self.task_stopping_event.is_set():

         try:

         except Exception as e:

             next_periodic_db_update_time = now + datetime.timedelta(seconds=dom_info_update_periodic_secs)

45. # Cache for thread-specific loggers to avoid creating multiple loggers for the same thread

48. def get_syslog_identifier_common():
49.     """Get syslog identifier based on current thread name, fallback to 'xcvrd_common'"""
50.     try:
51.         current_thread = threading.current_thread()
52.         thread_name = getattr(current_thread, 'name', None)
53.         if thread_name and thread_name != 'MainThread':
54.             return thread_name
55.     except Exception:
56.         pass
57.     return "xcvrd_common"

59. def get_helper_logger():
60.     """Get a thread-specific logger, creating one if it doesn't exist"""
61.     thread_id = threading.current_thread().ident
62.     thread_name = get_syslog_identifier_common()
63. 
64.     # Use thread_id as key to ensure thread safety
65.     if thread_id not in thread_loggers:
66.         thread_loggers[thread_id] = syslogger.SysLogger(thread_name, enable_runtime_config=True)
67. 
68.     return thread_loggers[thread_id]

70. # Create a module-level attribute that acts like a dynamic property
71. class HelperLoggerProxy:
72.     def __getattr__(self, name):

75. helper_logger = HelperLoggerProxy()

106.     for tb_line in msg:

153. def is_syncd_warm_restore_complete(namespace=''):
154.     """
155.     This function determines whether syncd's restore count is not 0, which indicates warm-reboot
156.     to avoid premature config push by xcvrd that caused port flaps.
157.     
158.     Args:
159.         namespace: The namespace (asic) to check. Empty string for single-ASIC or default namespace.
160.                    For multi-ASIC systems, pass the specific namespace (e.g., 'asic0', 'asic1').
161.     """
162.     state_db = daemon_base.db_connect("STATE_DB", namespace=namespace)
163.     restore_count = state_db.hget("WARM_RESTART_TABLE|syncd", "restore_count")
164.     system_enabled = state_db.hget("WARM_RESTART_ENABLE_TABLE|system", "enable")

167.         if restore_count is not None:

169.                 if restore_count > 0:
170.                     return True
171.             elif isinstance(restore_count, str):
172.                 if restore_count.strip().isdigit() and int(restore_count.strip()) > 0:
173.                     return True
174. 
175.         # --- Handle system_enabled (only care about "true"/"false"/None) ---
176.         if isinstance(system_enabled, str):
177.             if system_enabled.strip().lower() == "true":
178.                 return True

180.     except Exception as e:

216.         speed = 50000
217.     elif '40G' in ifname or 'XLAUI' in ifname or 'XLPPI' in ifname:
218.         speed = 40000

220.         speed = 25000
221.     elif '10G' in ifname or 'SFI' in ifname or 'XFI' in ifname:

253.         get_interface_speed(app_info.get('host_electrical_interface_id')) == speed):
254.             return (index & 0xf)

256.     helper_logger.log_notice(f'No application found from {appl_dict} with host_lane_count={host_lane_count} speed={speed}')

and arguments as a tuple.

translation happens, there's technically room to add new HAL methods, but the intent seems to be keeping
platform-bridge as a proven, stable interface. So I need to flag which
capabilities are already typed versus which ones require either new bridge methods or the call
_json workaround.

59.             logger (Logger): Logger object

61.             port_change_event_handler (function): Callback function to handle port change event

63.             the DB name and table name to monitor
64.         """
65.         # To avoid duplicate event processing, this dict stores the latest port
66.         # change event for each key which is a tuple of
67.         # (port_name, port_tbl.db_name, port_tbl.table_name)

116.     def handle_port_update_event(self, timeout=SELECT_TIMEOUT_MSECS):
117.         """
118.         Select PORT update events, notify the observers upon a port update in CONFIG_DB
119.         or a XCVR insertion/removal in STATE_DB
120. 
121.         Returns:
122.             bool: True if there's at least one update event; False if there's no update event.
123.         """
124.         has_event = False
125.         if not self.stop_event.is_set():
126.             (state, _) = self.sel.select(timeout)
127.             if state == swsscommon.Select.TIMEOUT:
128.                 return has_event
129.             if state != swsscommon.Select.OBJECT:
130.                 self.logger.log_warning('sel.select() did not return swsscommon.Select.OBJECT')
131.                 return has_event
132. 
133.             port_event_cache = {}
134.             for port_tbl in self.asic_context.keys():
135.                 while True:
136.                     (port_name, op, fvp) = port_tbl.pop()
137.                     if not port_name:
138.                         break
139.  
140.                     fvp = dict(fvp) if fvp is not None else {}
141.                     role = fvp.get(multi_asic.PORT_ROLE, None)
142.                     if role:
143.                         # If an internal port is broken out on the fly using DPB,
144.                         # the assumption here is that we would recieve CONFIG_DB or APPL_DB notification before STATE_DB
145.                         self.port_role_map[port_name] = role
146.                     else:
147.                         # role attribute might not be present for state DB
148.                         # notifs and thus need to maintain a cache
149.                         role = self.port_role_map.get(port_name, None)
150. 
151.                     if not multi_asic.is_front_panel_port(port_name, role):
152.                         continue
153. 
154.                     self.logger.log_info("$$$ {} handle_port_update_event() : op={} DB:{} Table:{} fvp {}".format(
155.                                          port_name, op, port_tbl.db_name, port_tbl.table_name, fvp))
156.                     if 'index' not in fvp:
157.                        fvp['index'] = '-1'
158.                     fvp['port_name'] = port_name
159.                     fvp['asic_id'] = self.asic_context[port_tbl]
160.                     fvp['op'] = op
161.                     fvp['FILTER'] = port_tbl.filter
162.                     # Soak duplicate events and consider only the last event
163.                     port_event_cache[(port_name, port_tbl.db_name, port_tbl.table_name)] = fvp
164. 
165.             # Now apply filter over soaked events
166.             for key, fvp in port_event_cache.items():
167.                 db_name = key[1]
168.                 table_name = key[2]
169.                 port_index = int(fvp['index'])
170.                 port_change_event = None
171.                 filter = fvp['FILTER']
172.                 del fvp['FILTER']
173.                 self.apply_filter_to_fvp(filter, fvp)
174. 
175.                 if key in self.port_event_cache:
176.                     # Compare current event with last event on this key, to see if
177.                     # there's really a need to update.
178.                     diff = set(fvp.items()) - set(self.port_event_cache[key].items())
179.                     # Ignore duplicate events
180.                     if not diff:
181.                        self.port_event_cache[key] = fvp
182.                        continue
183.                 # Update the latest event to the cache
184.                 self.port_event_cache[key] = fvp
185. 
186.                 if fvp['op'] == swsscommon.SET_COMMAND:
187.                    port_change_event = PortChangeEvent(fvp['port_name'],
188.                                                             port_index,
189.                                                             fvp['asic_id'],
190.                                                             PortChangeEvent.PORT_SET,
191.                                                             fvp,
192.                                                             db_name,
193.                                                             table_name)
194.                 elif fvp['op'] == swsscommon.DEL_COMMAND:
195.                    port_change_event = PortChangeEvent(fvp['port_name'],
196.                                                             port_index,
197.                                                             fvp['asic_id'],
198.                                                             PortChangeEvent.PORT_DEL,
199.                                                             fvp,
200.                                                             db_name,
201.                                                             table_name)
202.                 # This is the final event considered for processing
203.                 self.logger.log_notice("*** {} handle_port_update_event() fvp {}".format(
204.                     key, fvp))
205.                 if port_change_event is not None:
206.                     has_event = True
207.                     self.port_change_event_handler(port_change_event)
208. 
209.         return has_event

213.     def __init__(self):
214.         # A list of logical port name, e.g. ["Ethernet0", "Ethernet4" ...]
215.         self.logical_port_list = []
216.         # Logical port name to physical port index mapping
217.         self.logical_to_physical = {}
218.         # Mapping of physical port indices to logical port names.
219.         # Each physical port index maps to a list of logical port names, which are sorted in natural order.
220.         # Example:
221.         # {
222.         #     0: ["Ethernet0", "Ethernet4"],  # Physical port 0 maps to logical ports Ethernet0 and Ethernet4
223.         #     1: ["Ethernet8", "Ethernet12"],  # Physical port 1 maps to logical ports Ethernet1 and Ethernet5
224.         # }
225.         self.physical_to_logical = {}
226.         # Logical port name to ASIC ID mapping
227.         self.logical_to_asic = {}
228. 
229.     def handle_port_change_event(self, port_change_event):
230.         if port_change_event.event_type == PortChangeEvent.PORT_ADD:
231.             self._handle_port_add(port_change_event)
232.         elif port_change_event.event_type == PortChangeEvent.PORT_REMOVE:
233.             self._handle_port_remove(port_change_event)
234. 
235.     def _handle_port_add(self, port_change_event):
236.         port_name = port_change_event.port_name
237.         self.logical_port_list.append(port_name)
238.         self.logical_to_physical[port_name] = port_change_event.port_index
239.         if port_change_event.port_index not in self.physical_to_logical:
240.             self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index] = [port_name]
241.         else:
242.             # Append the new logical port and sort the list
243.             self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index].append(port_name)
244. 
245.             self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index] = natsorted(
246.                 self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index], key=lambda x: x.lower()
247.             )
248. 
249.         self.logical_to_asic[port_name] = port_change_event.asic_id
250. 
251.     def _handle_port_remove(self, port_change_event):
252.         port_name = port_change_event.port_name
253.         self.logical_port_list.remove(port_name)
254.         self.logical_to_physical.pop(port_name)
255.         self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index].remove(port_name)
256.         if not self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index]:
257.             self.physical_to_logical.pop(port_change_event.port_index)
258.         self.logical_to_asic.pop(port_name)
259. 
260.     def get_asic_id_for_logical_port(self, port_name):
261.         return self.logical_to_asic.get(port_name)
262. 
263.     def is_logical_port(self, port_name):
264.         return port_name in self.logical_to_physical
265. 
266.     def get_logical_to_physical(self, port_name):
267.         port_index = self.logical_to_physical.get(port_name)
268.         return None if port_index is None else [port_index]
269. 
270.     def get_physical_to_logical(self, physical_port: int):
271.         assert isinstance(physical_port, int), "{} is NOT integer".format(physical_port)
272.         return self.physical_to_logical.get(physical_port)
273. 
274.     def logical_port_name_to_physical_port_list(self, port_name):
275.         try:
276.             return [int(port_name)]
277.         except ValueError:
278.             if self.is_logical_port(port_name):
279.                 return self.get_logical_to_physical(port_name)
280.             else:
281.                 return None

         or a XCVR insertion/removal in STATE_DB
 
         Returns:
             bool: True if there's at least one update event; False if there's no update event.
         """
         has_event = False
         if not self.stop_event.is_set():
             (state, _) = self.sel.select(timeout)
             if state == swsscommon.Select.TIMEOUT:
                 return has_event
             if state != swsscommon.Select.OBJECT:
                 self.logger.log_warning('sel.select() did not return swsscommon.Select.OBJECT')
                 return has_event
 
             port_event_cache = {}
             for port_tbl in self.asic_context.keys():
                 while True:
                     (port_name, op, fvp) = port_tbl.pop()
                     if not port_name:
                         break
  
                     fvp = dict(fvp) if fvp is not None else {}
                     role = fvp.get(multi_asic.PORT_ROLE, None)
                     if role:
                         # If an internal port is broken out on the fly using DPB,
                         # the assumption here is that we would recieve CONFIG_DB or APPL_DB notification before STATE_DB
                         self.port_role_map[port_name] = role
                     else:
                         # role attribute might not be present for state DB
                         # notifs and thus need to maintain a cache
                         role = self.port_role_map.get(port_name, None)
 
                     if not multi_asic.is_front_panel_port(port_name, role):
                         continue
 
                     self.logger.log_info("$$$ {} handle_port_update_event() : op={} DB:{} Table:{} fvp {}".format(
                                          port_name, op, port_tbl.db_name, port_tbl.table_name, fvp))
                     if 'index' not in fvp:
                        fvp['index'] = '-1'
                     fvp['port_name'] = port_name
                     fvp['asic_id'] = self.asic_context[port_tbl]
                     fvp['op'] = op
                     fvp['FILTER'] = port_tbl.filter
                     # Soak duplicate events and consider only the last event
                     port_event_cache[(port_name, port_tbl.db_name, port_tbl.table_name)] = fvp
 
             # Now apply filter over soaked events
             for key, fvp in port_event_cache.items():
                 db_name = key[1]
                 table_name = key[2]
                 port_index = int(fvp['index'])
                 port_change_event = None
                 filter = fvp['FILTER']
                 del fvp['FILTER']
                 self.apply_filter_to_fvp(filter, fvp)
 
                 if key in self.port_event_cache:
                     # Compare current event with last event on this key, to see if
                     # there's really a need to update.
                     diff = set(fvp.items()) - set(self.port_event_cache[key].items())
                     # Ignore duplicate events
                     if not diff:
                        self.port_event_cache[key] = fvp
                        continue
                 # Update the latest event to the cache
                 self.port_event_cache[key] = fvp
 
                 if fvp['op'] == swsscommon.SET_COMMAND:
                    port_change_event = PortChangeEvent(fvp['port_name'],
                                                             port_index,
                                                             fvp['asic_id'],
                                                             PortChangeEvent.PORT_SET,
                                                             fvp,
                                                             db_name,
                                                             table_name)
                 elif fvp['op'] == swsscommon.DEL_COMMAND:
                    port_change_event = PortChangeEvent(fvp['port_name'],
                                                             port_index,
                                                             fvp['asic_id'],
                                                             PortChangeEvent.PORT_DEL,
                                                             fvp,
                                                             db_name,
                                                             table_name)
                 # This is the final event considered for processing
                 self.logger.log_notice("*** {} handle_port_update_event() fvp {}".format(
                     key, fvp))
                 if port_change_event is not None:
                     has_event = True
                     self.port_change_event_handler(port_change_event)
 
         return has_event
 
 
 class PortMapping:
     def __init__(self):
         # A list of logical port name, e.g. ["Ethernet0", "Ethernet4" ...]
         self.logical_port_list = []
         # Logical port name to physical port index mapping
         self.logical_to_physical = {}
         # Mapping of physical port indices to logical port names.
         # Each physical port index maps to a list of logical port names, which are sorted in natural order.
         # Example:
         # {
         #     0: ["Ethernet0", "Ethernet4"],  # Physical port 0 maps to logical ports Ethernet0 and Ethernet4
         #     1: ["Ethernet8", "Ethernet12"],  # Physical port 1 maps to logical ports Ethernet1 and Ethernet5
         # }
         self.physical_to_logical = {}
         # Logical port name to ASIC ID mapping
         self.logical_to_asic = {}
 
     def handle_port_change_event(self, port_change_event):
         if port_change_event.event_type == PortChangeEvent.PORT_ADD:
             self._handle_port_add(port_change_event)
         elif port_change_event.event_type == PortChangeEvent.PORT_REMOVE:
             self._handle_port_remove(port_change_event)
 
     def _handle_port_add(self, port_change_event):
         port_name = port_change_event.port_name
         self.logical_port_list.append(port_name)
         self.logical_to_physical[port_name] = port_change_event.port_index
         if port_change_event.port_index not in self.physical_to_logical:
             self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index] = [port_name]
         else:
             # Append the new logical port and sort the list
             self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index].append(port_name)
 
             self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index] = natsorted(
                 self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index], key=lambda x: x.lower()
             )
 
         self.logical_to_asic[port_name] = port_change_event.asic_id
 
     def _handle_port_remove(self, port_change_event):
         port_name = port_change_event.port_name
         self.logical_port_list.remove(port_name)
         self.logical_to_physical.pop(port_name)
         self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index].remove(port_name)
         if not self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index]:
             self.physical_to_logical.pop(port_change_event.port_index)
         self.logical_to_asic.pop(port_name)
 
     def get_asic_id_for_logical_port(self, port_name):
         return self.logical_to_asic.get(port_name)
 
     def is_logical_port(self, port_name):
         return port_name in self.logical_to_physical
 
     def get_logical_to_physical(self, port_name):
         port_index = self.logical_to_physical.get(port_name)
         return None if port_index is None else [port_index]
 
     def get_physical_to_logical(self, physical_port: int):
         assert isinstance(physical_port, int), "{} is NOT integer".format(physical_port)
         return self.physical_to_logical.get(physical_port)
 
     def logical_port_name_to_physical_port_list(self, port_name):
         try:
             return [int(port_name)]
         except ValueError:
             if self.is_logical_port(port_name):
                 return self.get_logical_to_physical(port_name)
             else:
                 return None
 
 def subscribe_port_config_change(namespaces):
     sel = swsscommon.Select()
     asic_context = {}
     for namespace in namespaces:
         config_db = daemon_base.db_connect("CONFIG_DB", namespace=namespace)
         asic_id = multi_asic.get_asic_index_from_namespace(namespace)
         port_tbl = swsscommon.SubscriberStateTable(config_db, swsscommon.CFG_PORT_TABLE_NAME)
         asic_context[port_tbl] = asic_id
         sel.addSelectable(port_tbl)
     return sel, asic_context
 
 def handle_port_config_change(sel, asic_context, stop_event, port_mapping, logger, port_change_event_handler):
     """Select CONFIG_DB PORT table changes, once there is a port configuration add/remove, notify observers
     """
     if not stop_event.is_set():
         (state, _) = sel.select(SELECT_TIMEOUT_MSECS)
         if state == swsscommon.Select.TIMEOUT:
             return
         if state != swsscommon.Select.OBJECT:
             logger.log_warning('sel.select() did not return swsscommon.Select.OBJECT')
             return
 
         read_port_config_change(asic_context, port_mapping, logger, port_change_event_handler)
 
 def read_port_config_change(asic_context, port_mapping, logger, port_change_event_handler):
     for port_tbl in asic_context.keys():
         while True:
             (key, op, fvp) = port_tbl.pop()
             if not key:
                 break
             fvp = dict(fvp)
             if not multi_asic.is_front_panel_port(key, fvp.get(multi_asic.PORT_ROLE, None)):
                 continue
             if op == swsscommon.SET_COMMAND:
                 if 'index' not in fvp:
                     continue
 
                 new_physical_index = int(fvp['index'])
                 if not port_mapping.is_logical_port(key):
                     # New logical port created
                     port_change_event = PortChangeEvent(key, new_physical_index, asic_context[port_tbl], PortChangeEvent.PORT_ADD)
                     port_change_event_handler(port_change_event)
                 else:
                     current_physical_index = port_mapping.get_logical_to_physical(key)[0]
                     if current_physical_index != new_physical_index:
                         port_change_event = PortChangeEvent(key,
                                                             current_physical_index,
                                                             asic_context[port_tbl],
                                                             PortChangeEvent.PORT_REMOVE)
                         port_change_event_handler(port_change_event)
 
                         port_change_event = PortChangeEvent(key, new_physical_index, asic_context[port_tbl], PortChangeEvent.PORT_ADD)
                         port_change_event_handler(port_change_event)
             elif op == swsscommon.DEL_COMMAND:
                 if port_mapping.is_logical_port(key):
                     port_change_event = PortChangeEvent(key,
                                                         port_mapping.get_logical_to_physical(key)[0],
                                                         asic_context[port_tbl],
                                                         PortChangeEvent.PORT_REMOVE)
                     port_change_event_handler(port_change_event)
             else:
                 logger.log_warning('Invalid DB operation: {}'.format(op))
 
 def get_port_mapping(namespaces):
     """Get port mapping from CONFIG_DB
     """
     port_mapping = PortMapping()
     for namespace in namespaces:
         asic_id = multi_asic.get_asic_index_from_namespace(namespace)
         config_db = daemon_base.db_connect("CONFIG_DB", namespace=namespace)
         port_table = swsscommon.Table(config_db, swsscommon.CFG_PORT_TABLE_NAME)
         for key in port_table.getKeys():
             _, port_config = port_table.get(key)
             port_config_dict = dict(port_config)
             if not multi_asic.is_front_panel_port(key, port_config_dict.get(multi_asic.PORT_ROLE, None)):
                 continue
             port_change_event = PortChangeEvent(key, port_config_dict['index'], asic_id, PortChangeEvent.PORT_ADD)
             port_mapping.handle_port_change_event(port_change_event)
     return port_mapping

 # Thread wrapper class for SFF compliant transceiver management
 class SffManagerTask(threading.Thread):
 
     # CONFIG_DB port table fields:
 
     ADMIN_STATUS = 'admin_status'

     XCVR_TYPE = 'type'

     HOST_TX_READY = 'host_tx_ready'

         },

             'STATE_DB': 'PORT_TABLE',

     SFF_LOGGER_PREFIX = "SFF-MAIN: "

1. """StateDB: thin wrapper over ``sonic-db-cli`` for black-box observation.
2. 
3. Tests read xcvrd's declared outputs (the TRANSCEIVER_* tables) from STATE_DB.
4. We shell out to sonic-db-cli rather than importing swsscommon so the harness has
5. zero binary dependencies on the DUT host (sonic-db-cli is always present, and it
6. reaches the same redis xcvrd writes to). Calls are ~50-100ms which is fine for
7. the polling cadence the black-box assertions use.
8. """
9. import subprocess
10. 
11. SONIC_DB_CLI = "/usr/bin/sonic-db-cli"
12. 
13. 
14. class StateDB:
15.     def __init__(self, db="STATE_DB", binary=SONIC_DB_CLI):
16.         self.db = db
17.         self.binary = binary
18. 
19.     def _run(self, *args):
20.         out = subprocess.run(
21.             [self.binary, self.db, *[str(a) for a in args]],
22.             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
23.         if out.returncode != 0:
24.             raise RuntimeError(
25.                 f"sonic-db-cli {self.db} {' '.join(map(str, args))} failed: "
26.                 f"{out.stderr.strip()}")
27.         # CMIS string fields are fixed-width, null-padded by the emulator (real
28.         # modules space-pad). Those NUL bytes are padding artifacts, never real
29.         # data, and they break ast.literal_eval on HGETALL output -- strip them.
30.         return out.stdout.replace("\x00", "")
31. 
32.     # --- reads --------------------------------------------------------------
33.     def keys(self, pattern):
34.         out = self._run("KEYS", pattern).strip()
35.         return [k for k in out.splitlines() if k]
36. 
37.     def exists(self, key):
38.         return self._run("EXISTS", key).strip() == "1"
39. 
40.     def hget(self, key, field):
41.         val = self._run("HGET", key, field).rstrip("\n")
42.         return val if val != "" else None
43. 
44.     def hgetall(self, key):
45.         """Return the hash as a dict (empty dict if the key is absent)."""
46.         out = self._run("HGETALL", key)
47.         text = out.strip()
48.         # sonic-db-cli prints a Python-dict repr for HGETALL.
49.         if text.startswith("{") and text.endswith("}"):
50.             import ast
51.             try:
52.                 return dict(ast.literal_eval(text))
53.             except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
54.                 pass
55.         # Fallback: alternating key/value lines.
56.         toks = [t for t in text.split("\n") if t != ""]
57.         return {toks[i]: toks[i + 1] for i in range(0, len(toks) - 1, 2)}
58. 
59.     # --- writes (used only for test setup/teardown, e.g. flush / inject) -----
60.     def hset(self, key, field, value):
61.         v = str(value)
62.         if v.startswith("-"):
63.             # sonic-db-cli's arg parser treats a leading-'-' value as an unknown
64.             # option; the '--' guard forces the value to be parsed as positional.
65.             return self._run("HSET", key, field, "--", v)
66.         return self._run("HSET", key, field, v)
67. 
68.     def hdel(self, key, field):
69.         return self._run("HDEL", key, field)
70. 
71.     def delete(self, key):
72.         return self._run("DEL", key)
73. 
74.     def delete_pattern(self, pattern):
75.         n = 0
76.         for k in self.keys(pattern):
77.             self.delete(k)
78.             n += 1
79.         return n
80.

1. """TRANSCEIVER_INFO content correctness (HLD 1.1.1).
2. 
3. The static identity xcvrd publishes must match what the emulator serves. The
4. emulator's emu_config.yaml defines VendorName=xcvr-emu, VendorPN=EMU-40G-LR4,
5. VendorSN=0123456789, VendorOUI=0x010203, QSFP-DD / CMIS 5.2, Power Class 8.
6. These are the oracle values for the fields below.
7. """
8. from lib.waits import T_FAST, T_MULTI, wait_until, T_DOM
9. import pytest
10. 
11. 
12. def test_info_has_expected_identity(module):
13.     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
14.     info = module.info()
15.     assert info.get("manufacturer") == "xcvr-emu"
16.     assert info.get("model") == "EMU-40G-LR4"
17.     assert info.get("vendor_oui") == "01-02-03"
18. 
19. 
20. def test_info_serial_and_revision(module):
21.     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
22.     info = module.info()
23.     assert info.get("serial") == "0123456789"
24.     assert info.get("vendor_rev") in ("01", "1")
25. 
26. 
27. def test_info_type_is_qsfp_dd(module):
28.     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
29.     info = module.info()
30.     type_str = (info.get("type") or "").upper()
31.     assert "QSFP" in type_str and "DD" in type_str, f"unexpected type={info.get('type')!r}"
32. 
33. 
34. def test_info_power_class(module):
35.     """ext_identifier should reflect the configured Power Class 8."""
36.     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
37.     info = module.info()
38.     ext = info.get("ext_identifier") or ""
39.     assert "Power Class 8" in ext, f"unexpected ext_identifier={ext!r}"
40. 
41. 
42. def test_all_present_ports_have_info(emu, statedb, configdb):
43.     """Every emulator module whose logical port exists in CONFIG_DB and is
44.     admin-up should converge to a populated TRANSCEIVER_INFO row."""
45.     from lib.emu import index_to_port
46.     from lib.waits import wait_until
47.     ports = []
48.     for idx, is_present in emu.list().items():
49.         if not is_present:
50.             continue
51.         port = index_to_port(idx)
52.         if configdb.hget(f"PORT|{port}", "admin_status") == "up":
53.             ports.append(port)
54.     if not ports:
55.         import pytest
56.         pytest.skip("no admin-up emulator-backed ports found in CONFIG_DB")
57. 
58.     def _all_populated():
59.         return all(statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{p}", "manufacturer") for p in ports)
60.     wait_until(_all_populated, timeout=T_MULTI,
61.                msg=f"all {len(ports)} admin-up ports populated")
62. 
63.     for port in ports:
64.         assert statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "manufacturer") == "xcvr-emu", \
65.             f"{port} has unexpected manufacturer"
66. 
67. 
68. def test_info_extended_identity(module):
69.     """Rich static identity fields decode to the emulator's oracle values -- not
70.     just manufacturer/model/serial. A daemon that stubs these fails the parity."""
71.     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
72.     info = module.info()
73.     assert "MPO" in (info.get("connector") or ""), f"connector={info.get('connector')!r}"
74.     assert info.get("cable_length") == "100.0", f"cable_length={info.get('cable_length')!r}"
75.     assert info.get("cmis_rev") == "5.2", f"cmis_rev={info.get('cmis_rev')!r}"
76.     assert info.get("type_abbrv_name") == "QSFP-DD", f"type_abbrv_name={info.get('type_abbrv_name')!r}"
77.     assert info.get("specification_compliance") == "sm_media_interface", \
78.         f"specification_compliance={info.get('specification_compliance')!r}"
79.     assert info.get("is_replaceable") == "True", f"is_replaceable={info.get('is_replaceable')!r}"
80.     assert info.get("vdm_supported") == "False", f"vdm_supported={info.get('vdm_supported')!r}"
81.     assert (info.get("vendor_date") or "").startswith("2024-12-14"), \
82.         f"vendor_date={info.get('vendor_date')!r}"
83.     assert info.get("media_interface_technology"), "media_interface_technology missing"
84. 
85. 
86. def test_info_application_advertisement(module):
87.     """application_advertisement is a real, structured CMIS application list (per
88.     entry: host/media interface ids + host/media lane counts), not empty or N/A."""
89.     import ast
90.     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
91.     adv = module.info().get("application_advertisement")
92.     assert adv and adv != "N/A", f"application_advertisement={adv!r}"
93.     parsed = ast.literal_eval(adv)
94.     assert isinstance(parsed, dict) and parsed, f"unparseable/empty advertisement: {adv!r}"
95.     first = next(iter(parsed.values()))
96.     assert "host_lane_count" in first and "media_lane_count" in first, \
97.         f"advertisement entry missing lane counts: {first!r}"
98. 
99. 
100. def test_info_apsel_and_lane_count_on_activated_port(emu, statedb, configdb):
101.     """On an admin-up (datapath-activated) port, xcvrd writes REAL host/media lane
102.     counts + per-host-lane application-select into TRANSCEIVER_INFO (these read N/A
103.     on the admin-down baseline; the CMIS manager fills them after DP activation)."""
104.     from lib.emu import index_to_port
105.     port = None
106.     for idx, present in sorted(emu.list().items()):
107.         if present and configdb.hget(f"PORT|{index_to_port(idx)}", "admin_status") == "up":
108.             port = index_to_port(idx)
109.             break
110.     if port is None:
111.         pytest.skip("no admin-up emulator-backed port")
112. 
113.     wait_until(lambda: statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "host_lane_count") not in (None, "N/A"),
114.                timeout=T_DOM, msg=f"{port} host_lane_count becomes real after datapath activation")
115.     n = int(statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "host_lane_count"))
116.     assert n >= 1, f"{port} host_lane_count={n!r}"
117.     assert statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "media_lane_count") not in (None, "N/A"), \
118.         f"{port} media_lane_count is N/A on an activated port"
119.     assert statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "active_apsel_hostlane1") not in (None, "N/A"), \
120.         f"{port} active_apsel_hostlane1 is N/A on an activated port"
121.

--- a/home/sonic/dev/sonic-dev/xcvrd-tests/tests/test_info_content.py
+++ b/home/sonic/dev/sonic-dev/xcvrd-tests/tests/test_info_content.py
@@ -1,121 +1,121 @@
 """TRANSCEIVER_INFO content correctness (HLD 1.1.1).
 
 The static identity xcvrd publishes must match what the emulator serves. The
 emulator's emu_config.yaml defines VendorName=xcvr-emu, VendorPN=EMU-40G-LR4,
 VendorSN=0123456789, VendorOUI=0x010203, QSFP-DD / CMIS 5.2, Power Class 8.
 These are the oracle values for the fields below.
 """
 from lib.waits import T_FAST, T_MULTI, wait_until, T_DOM
 import pytest
 
 
 def test_info_has_expected_identity(module):
     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
     info = module.info()
     assert info.get("manufacturer") == "xcvr-emu"
     assert info.get("model") == "EMU-40G-LR4"
     assert info.get("vendor_oui") == "01-02-03"
 
 
 def test_info_serial_and_revision(module):
     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
     info = module.info()
     assert info.get("serial") == "0123456789"
     assert info.get("vendor_rev") in ("01", "1")
 
 
 def test_info_type_is_qsfp_dd(module):
     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
     info = module.info()
     type_str = (info.get("type") or "").upper()
     assert "QSFP" in type_str and "DD" in type_str, f"unexpected type={info.get('type')!r}"
 
 
 def test_info_power_class(module):
     """ext_identifier should reflect the configured Power Class 8."""
     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
     info = module.info()
     ext = info.get("ext_identifier") or ""
     assert "Power Class 8" in ext, f"unexpected ext_identifier={ext!r}"
 
 
 def test_all_present_ports_have_info(emu, statedb, configdb):
     """Every emulator module whose logical port exists in CONFIG_DB and is
     admin-up should converge to a populated TRANSCEIVER_INFO row."""
     from lib.emu import index_to_port
     from lib.waits import wait_until
     ports = []
     for idx, is_present in emu.list().items():
         if not is_present:
             continue
         port = index_to_port(idx)
         if configdb.hget(f"PORT|{port}", "admin_status") == "up":
             ports.append(port)
     if not ports:
         import pytest
         pytest.skip("no admin-up emulator-backed ports found in CONFIG_DB")
 
     def _all_populated():
         return all(statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{p}", "manufacturer") for p in ports)
     wait_until(_all_populated, timeout=T_MULTI,
                msg=f"all {len(ports)} admin-up ports populated")
 
     for port in ports:
         assert statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "manufacturer") == "xcvr-emu", \
             f"{port} has unexpected manufacturer"
 
 
 def test_info_extended_identity(module):
     """Rich static identity fields decode to the emulator's oracle values -- not
     just manufacturer/model/serial. A daemon that stubs these fails the parity."""
     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
     info = module.info()
     assert "MPO" in (info.get("connector") or ""), f"connector={info.get('connector')!r}"
     assert info.get("cable_length") == "100.0", f"cable_length={info.get('cable_length')!r}"
     assert info.get("cmis_rev") == "5.2", f"cmis_rev={info.get('cmis_rev')!r}"
     assert info.get("type_abbrv_name") == "QSFP-DD", f"type_abbrv_name={info.get('type_abbrv_name')!r}"
     assert info.get("specification_compliance") == "sm_media_interface", \
         f"specification_compliance={info.get('specification_compliance')!r}"
     assert info.get("is_replaceable") == "True", f"is_replaceable={info.get('is_replaceable')!r}"
     assert info.get("vdm_supported") == "False", f"vdm_supported={info.get('vdm_supported')!r}"
     assert (info.get("vendor_date") or "").startswith("2024-12-14"), \
         f"vendor_date={info.get('vendor_date')!r}"
     assert info.get("media_interface_technology"), "media_interface_technology missing"
 
 
 def test_info_application_advertisement(module):
     """application_advertisement is a real, structured CMIS application list (per
     entry: host/media interface ids + host/media lane counts), not empty or N/A."""
     import ast
     module.wait_info_populated(timeout=T_FAST)
     adv = module.info().get("application_advertisement")
     assert adv and adv != "N/A", f"application_advertisement={adv!r}"
     parsed = ast.literal_eval(adv)
     assert isinstance(parsed, dict) and parsed, f"unparseable/empty advertisement: {adv!r}"
     first = next(iter(parsed.values()))
     assert "host_lane_count" in first and "media_lane_count" in first, \
         f"advertisement entry missing lane counts: {first!r}"
 
 
 def test_info_apsel_and_lane_count_on_activated_port(emu, statedb, configdb):
     """On an admin-up (datapath-activated) port, xcvrd writes REAL host/media lane
     counts + per-host-lane application-select into TRANSCEIVER_INFO (these read N/A
     on the admin-down baseline; the CMIS manager fills them after DP activation)."""
     from lib.emu import index_to_port
     port = None
     for idx, present in sorted(emu.list().items()):
         if present and configdb.hget(f"PORT|{index_to_port(idx)}", "admin_status") == "up":
             port = index_to_port(idx)
             break
     if port is None:
         pytest.skip("no admin-up emulator-backed port")
 
     wait_until(lambda: statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "host_lane_count") not in (None, "N/A"),
                timeout=T_DOM, msg=f"{port} host_lane_count becomes real after datapath activation")
     n = int(statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "host_lane_count"))
     assert n >= 1, f"{port} host_lane_count={n!r}"
     assert statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "media_lane_count") not in (None, "N/A"), \
         f"{port} media_lane_count is N/A on an activated port"
     assert statedb.hget(f"TRANSCEIVER_INFO|{port}", "active_apsel_hostlane1") not in (None, "N/A"), \
         f"{port} active_apsel_hostlane1 is N/A on an activated port"

 """Rich TRANSCEIVER_STATUS table coverage (module + per-lane datapath state).
 
 xcvrd's DomInfoUpdateTask publishes TRANSCEIVER_STATUS with the CMIS module state
 and per-host-lane datapath / config / tx-rx state. For the admin-down baseline
 test port this reads the DEACTIVATED state (ModuleLowPwr / DataPathDeactivated);
 the ACTIVATED case (admin-up port) is covered by test_cmis_datapath.py. A
 candidate daemon that only publishes TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW (not the rich STATUS)
 fails here.
 """
 import pytest
 
 from lib.waits import wait_until, T_DOM
 
 pytestmark = pytest.mark.slow
 
 DP_STATES = [f"DP{i}State" for i in range(1, 9)]
 CONFIG_STATES = [f"config_state_hostlane{i}" for i in range(1, 9)]
 
 
 def _status_published(module):
     module.plug()
     wait_until(lambda: module.status().get("module_state"), timeout=T_DOM,
                msg=f"{module.port} TRANSCEIVER_STATUS published")
     return module.status()
 
 
 def test_status_table_published(module):
     """xcvrd publishes the rich STATUS table with the module + all 8 datapath fields."""
     st = _status_published(module)
     assert st.get("module_state"), f"module_state missing: {st}"
     assert "module_fault_cause" in st, "module_fault_cause missing from TRANSCEIVER_STATUS"
     for f in DP_STATES + CONFIG_STATES:
         assert f in st, f"{f} missing from TRANSCEIVER_STATUS"
 
 
 def test_status_baseline_deactivated(module, configdb):
     """Admin-down baseline: module in low power, every datapath deactivated."""
     if configdb.hget(f"PORT|{module.port}", "admin_status") == "up":
         pytest.skip(f"{module.port} is admin-up; the deactivated-baseline check is for "
                     "admin-down ports (activated case is in test_cmis_datapath.py)")
     st = _status_published(module)
     assert st.get("module_state") == "ModuleLowPwr", \
         f"module_state={st.get('module_state')!r} (expected ModuleLowPwr for admin-down {module.port})"
     for f in DP_STATES:
         assert st.get(f) == "DataPathDeactivated", f"{f}={st.get(f)!r} (expected DataPathDeactivated)"

15.

17. def _error(module):

20.

23.

26. def test_blocking_error_sets_status_and_removes_dom(module, inject):
27.     """I2C-stuck (blocking) -> STATUS_SW.error set, DOM removed, INFO kept."""

1. """MonitorRecorder: capture the xcvrd <-> emulator interaction trace.
2. 
3. The emulator implements a server-streaming ``Monitor`` RPC that emits one
4. message for *every* EEPROM Read and Write it serves. Since xcvrd reaches the
5. emulated transceivers exclusively through those reads/writes (via the bridge),
6. subscribing to this stream gives us a complete, timestamped trace of xcvrd's
7. interaction with the "hardware" -- with zero changes to xcvrd or the emulator.
8. 
9. Usage:
10.     rec = MonitorRecorder(); rec.start()
11.     ...stimulus...
12.     reads = rec.reads(index=25)          # all reads of module 25 so far
13.     rec.clear()                          # scope the next assertion window
14. """
15. import threading
16. import time
17. 
18. import grpc
19. 
20. from .proto import pb, pb_grpc
21. 
22. DEFAULT_TARGET = "localhost:50051"
23. 
24. 
25. class Event:
26.     __slots__ = ("ts", "index", "bank", "page", "offset", "length",
27.                  "data", "present", "write")
28. 
29.     def __init__(self, ts, msg):
30.         self.ts = ts
31.         self.index = msg.index
32.         self.bank = msg.bank
33.         self.page = msg.page
34.         self.offset = msg.offset
35.         self.length = msg.length
36.         self.data = bytes(msg.data)
37.         self.present = bool(msg.present)
38.         self.write = bool(msg.write)
39. 
40.     @property
41.     def is_read(self):
42.         return not self.write
43. 
44.     def __repr__(self):
45.         kind = "W" if self.write else "R"
46.         return (f"<{kind} idx={self.index} p{self.page:02x}h:"
47.                 f"{self.offset}+{self.length} data={self.data.hex()}>")
48. 
49. 
50. class MonitorRecorder:
51.     def __init__(self, target=DEFAULT_TARGET, index=0):
52.         # index=0 subscribes to ALL modules (the emulator filters on non-zero).
53.         self._target = target
54.         self._index = index
55.         self._events = []
56.         self._lock = threading.Lock()
57.         self._thread = None
58.         self._channel = None
59.         self._call = None
60.         self._stopping = False
61.         self._ready = threading.Event()
62. 
63.     # --- lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------------
64.     def start(self, ready_timeout=5.0):
65.         self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, name="mon-rec",
66.                                         daemon=True)
67.         self._thread.start()
68.         # Give the stream a moment to establish so early events aren't missed.
69.         self._ready.wait(timeout=ready_timeout)
70.         time.sleep(0.3)
71.         return self
72. 
73.     def stop(self):
74.         self._stopping = True
75.         try:
76.             if self._call is not None:
77.                 self._call.cancel()
78.         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
79.             pass
80.         try:
81.             if self._channel is not None:
82.                 self._channel.close()
83.         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
84.             pass
85.         if self._thread is not None:
86.             self._thread.join(timeout=3.0)
87. 
88.     def _run(self):
89.         self._channel = grpc.insecure_channel(self._target)
90.         stub = pb_grpc.SfpEmulatorServiceStub(self._channel)
91.         self._call = stub.Monitor(pb.MonitorRequest(index=self._index))
92.         self._ready.set()
93.         try:
94.             for msg in self._call:
95.                 ev = Event(time.time(), msg)
96.                 with self._lock:
97.                     self._events.append(ev)
98.         except grpc.RpcError:
99.             pass  # cancelled on stop() or emulator restart
100. 
101.     # --- query API ----------------------------------------------------------
102.     def clear(self):
103.         with self._lock:
104.             self._events.clear()
105. 
106.     def all(self):
107.         with self._lock:
108.             return list(self._events)
109. 
110.     def _filter(self, want_write, index=None, page=None, since=None):
111.         with self._lock:
112.             evs = list(self._events)

 """MonitorRecorder: capture the xcvrd <-> emulator interaction trace.
 
 The emulator implements a server-streaming ``Monitor`` RPC that emits one
 message for *every* EEPROM Read and Write it serves. Since xcvrd reaches the
 emulated transceivers exclusively through those reads/writes (via the bridge),
 subscribing to this stream gives us a complete, timestamped trace of xcvrd's
 interaction with the "hardware" -- with zero changes to xcvrd or the emulator.
 
 Usage:
     rec = MonitorRecorder(); rec.start()
     ...stimulus...
     reads = rec.reads(index=25)          # all reads of module 25 so far
     rec.clear()                          # scope the next assertion window
 """
 import threading
 import time
 
 import grpc
 
 from .proto import pb, pb_grpc
 
 DEFAULT_TARGET = "localhost:50051"
 
 
 class Event:
     __slots__ = ("ts", "index", "bank", "page", "offset", "length",
                  "data", "present", "write")
 
     def __init__(self, ts, msg):
         self.ts = ts
         self.index = msg.index
         self.bank = msg.bank
         self.page = msg.page
         self.offset = msg.offset
         self.length = msg.length
         self.data = bytes(msg.data)
         self.present = bool(msg.present)
         self.write = bool(msg.write)
 
     @property
     def is_read(self):
         return not self.write
 
     def __repr__(self):
         kind = "W" if self.write else "R"
         return (f"<{kind} idx={self.index} p{self.page:02x}h:"
                 f"{self.offset}+{self.length} data={self.data.hex()}>")
 
 
 class MonitorRecorder:
     def __init__(self, target=DEFAULT_TARGET, index=0):
         # index=0 subscribes to ALL modules (the emulator filters on non-zero).
         self._target = target
         self._index = index
         self._events = []
         self._lock = threading.Lock()
         self._thread = None
         self._channel = None
         self._call = None
         self._stopping = False
         self._ready = threading.Event()
 
     # --- lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------------
     def start(self, ready_timeout=5.0):
         self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, name="mon-rec",
                                         daemon=True)
         self._thread.start()
         # Give the stream a moment to establish so early events aren't missed.
         self._ready.wait(timeout=ready_timeout)
         time.sleep(0.3)
         return self
 
     def stop(self):
         self._stopping = True
         try:
             if self._call is not None:
                 self._call.cancel()
         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
             pass
         try:
             if self._channel is not None:
                 self._channel.close()
         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
             pass
         if self._thread is not None:
             self._thread.join(timeout=3.0)
 
     def _run(self):
         self._channel = grpc.insecure_channel(self._target)
         stub = pb_grpc.SfpEmulatorServiceStub(self._channel)
         self._call = stub.Monitor(pb.MonitorRequest(index=self._index))
         self._ready.set()
         try:
             for msg in self._call:
                 ev = Event(time.time(), msg)
                 with self._lock:
                     self._events.append(ev)
         except grpc.RpcError:
             pass  # cancelled on stop() or emulator restart
 
     # --- query API ----------------------------------------------------------
     def clear(self):
         with self._lock:
             self._events.clear()
 
     def all(self):
         with self._lock:
             return list(self._events)
 
     def _filter(self, want_write, index=None, page=None, since=None):
         with self._lock:
             evs = list(self._events)
         out = []
         for e in evs:
             if e.write != want_write:
                 continue
             if index is not None and e.index != index:
                 continue
             if page is not None and e.page != page:
                 continue
             if since is not None and e.ts < since:
                 continue
             out.append(e)
         return out
 
     def reads(self, index=None, page=None, since=None):
         return self._filter(False, index=index, page=page, since=since)
 
     def writes(self, index=None, page=None, since=None):
         return self._filter(True, index=index, page=page, since=since)
 
     def count(self, index=None):
         with self._lock:
             if index is None:
                 return len(self._events)
             return sum(1 for e in self._events if e.index == index)

17. //!      terminal `cmis_state`) flows at t≈0 for already-present modules; the CMIS
18. //!      manager then adopts those READY ports without re-driving bring-up.
19. //!   6. Build [`DomInfoUpdateTask`] + [`CmisManagerTask`] and run each on its OWN
20. //!      `std::thread` (mirroring the Python daemon, which starts them as separate
21. //!      `threading.Thread`s). DOM re-reads every present, DOM-polling-enabled module's
22. //!      DOM monitors on the DOM cadence and publishes `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR` (+
23. //!      flag/status tables); CMIS owns `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW.cmis_state` (INSERTED ->
24. //!      ... -> READY / FAILED), the non-terminal window the DOM task gates on.

26. //! poll `get_change_event`, and dispatch plug/unplug/SFP-error. Keeping DOM + CMIS OFF
27. //! the change-event thread is what makes SFP-error delivery reliable: a single DOM pass
28. //! re-reads page 00h + rich status + DOM/status flags for every module (dozens of
29. //! bridge round-trips), and if it ran inline it would block `get_change_event` long
30. //! enough that an injected error is not polled within the e2e's fast window. The three
31. //! threads share the ONE PyO3 chassis + STATE_DB handles; the Python GIL (released
32. //! across every bridge gRPC / redis wait) and the STATE_DB `Mutex` serialize concurrent
33. //! access exactly as they do for the Python daemon's threads.

35. //! reports only *transitions* against a per-chassis `_event_cache` seeded LAZILY on the
36. //! chassis's FIRST `get_change_event`, and the emulator surfaces the `XCVR_EMU_INJECT`
37. //! error hash through its OWN `SonicV2Connector(use_unix_socket_path=True)`
38. //! (`Chassis._get_statedb`), which fail-caches `False` for the chassis lifetime if its
39. //! first construct/connect throws. That connector needs the process-global
40. //! `swsscommon.SonicDBConfig` resolved to map STATE_DB → unix socket. The Rust
41. //! `swss-common` bindings connect by db-id + socket and NEVER load that Python singleton
42. //! (unlike the reference daemon, which connects its DBs BY NAME via `daemon_base.db_connect`

44. //! `env::init_embedded_db_config` (single-ASIC clean by-name load; `initializeGlobalConfig()`
45. //! only under `multi_asic.is_multi_asic()`, so it never flips the singleton into namespace
46. //! mode without a `database_global.json`). That call runs at a clean single-threaded boot
47. //! point and VERIFIES the emulator's exact read path with bounded retries, so the emulator's
48. //! later `_get_statedb` cannot fail-cache for the `SonicDBConfig` reason. The daemon then makes
49. //! ONE boot-time `get_change_event` prime to seed the all-present `_event_cache` baseline BEFORE

51. //! injects only after BOTH its `wait_info_populated` and `_dom_present` gates open, and
